title: Lidar step-coherence off-catalogue scarp carpet (3DEP 1 m lidar couplet + shoreline/channel mimic features, hide-and-recover GBM, 3 px catalogue collar, 2.8 px Poisson-disc carpet)
hypothesis: Expert-mapped new faults in the GeoDAWN region are predominantly subtle topographic steps (piedmont scarps, bedrock lineaments, splays and continuations) visible in the 1 m 3DEP lidar but absent from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue. At 100 m they manifest as pixels with high lidar step amplitude (step_max), a paired convex/concave Laplacian couplet (lappos_max/lapneg_max = scarp crest and base), and along-strike coherence (coh100, oriented persistence). A gradient-boosted classifier trained to recover WITHHELD catalogue strands from these lidar signatures plus regional context ranks off-catalogue pixels; dots are emitted as a >= 2.8 px Poisson-disc carpet outside a 3 px catalogue collar (the dot economics of the DTI metric: alpha = 0.2 makes a non-redundant dot pay whenever its expected kernel credit exceeds 0.2 x DTI ~ 0.06).
mechanism: Quaternary normal faulting in alluvium produces metre-scale steps that persist along strike; the lidar step_max / Laplacian crest-base couplet captures the scarp cross-section, coherence and oriented persistence suppress isolated noise; the catalogue collar removes near-trace dots that the portal evidence (GEMSDOE81 cont_asb, 44,090 dots at median 2.2 px -> 0.0041 USER-REPORTED) shows are nearly worthless.
named_non_fault_mimics: Pluvial Lake Lahontan shorelines and recessional benches (level steps at <= ~1,340 m): discriminated by dem_mean elevation, local slope and relief context
Stream terrace risers and channel banks: discriminated by 10 m channel density (chan_n) and knickpoint counts (knick_n)
Roads, canals, railroad grades: straight low-relief steps; partially captured by strike/persistence features (residual risk, flagged)
Bedrock-alluvium range-front contacts without active faulting

derived_from_lidar: persist = max over 4 orientations of 5 px line mean of step_max

catalogue_features: NONE (zero-catalogue feature set). The catalogue enters only the emission mask (collar) and the training labels.
difference_from_repo_lanes: ADHR/TDKL/HGVC/VHGD used lidar bands inside 44-107-channel PoE stacks dominated by geophysical conduit framing; no lane isolated the lidar step couplet with a lidar-vs-no-lidar ablation as the decision variable, nor used shoreline-elevation and channel-density mimic features. H88-RELAY used catalogue geometry only; MTAS/XGCE/GZZC used potential fields only.
difference_from_sibling_sites: 7GEMSDOE lidarscarp-ridge-top2pct (0.1461), GEMSDOE64 h64-lidar-scarp-cv (0.0383), GEMSDOE47 h60-lidarscarp-s2p0 (0.0430), GEMSDOE66 lidar03-cvretrain-reliefdecile (0.1152) emitted ridge-percentile / threshold maps; none combined hide-and-recover GBM ranking with the 3 px collar + 2.8 px carpet economics and explicit mimic features.

evaluator.name: gems57-pooled-hide-v2
evaluator.folds: holdout.buffered_component_draw(seed in {20, 21}, hide_frac=0.20, buffer_px=3, boundary_px=12); leave-one-quadrant-out training on the visible catalogue of the other three quadrants
evaluator.scoring: pooled DTI alpha=0.2 beta=0.8 300 m triangular; visible catalogue pixel-exactly masked; subsets far (>10 px from visible) and blind (>25 px)
evaluator.bootstrap: paired physical 20 km block percentile, 1000 draws, seed 520810

experiments.what: single-feature leakage canary (symmetric AUC <= 0.90 per feature) + 8-cell holdout of arm A (LSC-36 features) vs arm B (organizer 19-band subset only, identical emitter) at fold-proportional budget 40,000 x region_cells / 5,167,373
experiments.decision: promote the lane only if arm A beats arm B on pooled overall AND far>10 px with a paired 95% CI excluding 0

experiments.what: spacing policy on the same surfaces: uniform 2.8 px vs adaptive (2.8 px for the top half of the budget, 4.0 px for the rest)
experiments.decision: choose the policy with the higher pooled overall DTI

experiments.what: production build: fit on the whole visible catalogue, 40,000 dots, 3 px collar; registry uniqueness; format validation; TIFF + ZIP + run card
experiments.decision: ok_to_submit requires: validator all checks pass, pre-placement |Spearman| <= 0.90 and like-for-like 3 px forward overlap <= 0.70 against every registry raster, share_le2 == 0, share_gt25 >= 0.35

uniqueness_rule.registry_dots_definition: binary/sparse registry rasters: their positive cells; dense/continuous registry rasters (positive on > 10% of the footprint): their top-k cells with k = our dot count AND their top-2% cells (the emission rate the 17GEMSDOE site itself used for its scored file); the worse of the two is binding
uniqueness_rule.rationale: The protocol rule is a lane-drift detector phrased for dot rasters. A probability raster positive on every footprint cell has no dots; reading every positive cell as a dot gives the test a 100% false-positive rate (it flags every possible raster, including every already-scored submission) and so carries no information about lane drift. Resolution of IR-88-86/113/114 is logged in IRREGULARITIES.md and flagged for review.

labels: HOLDOUT-DTI numbers carry evaluator version, withheld positive count and 95% CI; ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED only from a submission-page receipt (none exists for this lane); H33 0.2778 and leaderboard 0.4413 are USER-REPORTED / public-page snapshot.
